concept:framing-geometry.note: Accepted iteration: keep terminator-nadir. Midnight overhead is usually umbra; dark-site lighting is off-nadir and parked.
concept:framing-geometry.title: Dusk/dawn snapshot, not midnight
concept:framing-geometry.recommend: Keep terminator-nadir (sunlit dusk/dawn footpoint) as the brightness envelope, because a mirror overhead at local midnight is usually in Earth’s shadow and has nothing to bounce. Dark-city lighting is a different, parked geometry. Treat 18 m / 55 m / 1 km as scale markers, not architectures. Keep the 400–2000 km grid; GEO is a size check only.

concept:framing-question.title: The question
concept:framing-question.recommend: Freeze the question as: how bright, how big, and how long is the ground patch at dusk/dawn looking straight down? Then: does energy or the orbital shutter bind first. Lighting/PV wait until those numbers exist.

concept:framing-variables.title: What we vary vs what we freeze
concept:framing-variables.recommend: Vary only altitude, area, and optical factor. Keep fold 45° and nadir 90° as a frozen snapshot. Do not let lighting or PV thresholds choose the model.

concept:framing-glossary.title: The Sun is a disk, not a lamp
concept:framing-glossary.recommend: Treat the ground patch as the Sun’s image. Focusing cannot shrink it. Binders are energy (including that dilution) or shutter — not cost, not “spot too small.”

concept:framing-classes.title: How we will score uses later
concept:framing-classes.recommend: Keep moonlight / lighting / weak PV / energy / daylight as parked estimated bins for a later readout. They must not choose area, altitude, or efficiency.

concept:framing-scope.title: What we are not modeling
concept:framing-scope.recommend: Keep cost, clouds-as-peak-I, eclipse on the pass, 3D, daytime geometry, and company evaluation out of this version. Peak I stays a clear-sky envelope.

concept:spec-snapshot.title: Only one brightness geometry
concept:spec-snapshot.recommend: Keep kernel I at terminator-nadir only. The 30° elevation cut is for timing, not for dimming the quoted peak.

concept:spec-image.title: Patch size
concept:spec-image.recommend: Keep D = h × α with α the full solar angular diameter, the same for flat and focusing, computed in metres.

concept:spec-irradiance.title: Brightness formula
concept:spec-irradiance.recommend: Keep I as collected sunlight spread over the solar image (not a lamp 1/r²). Pass η as one factor (1 or 0.675); do not stack ρ and τ on top.

concept:spec-pass.title: How long a pass lasts
concept:spec-pass.recommend: Keep period on a = R_Earth + h. Useful time is geometric visibility above 30° on an overhead pass, with no umbra cut — an upper bound on duration.

concept:spec-derived.title: Energy per pass is an upper bound
concept:spec-derived.recommend: Keep fluence as I × T_useful, labeled upper bound. Keep required_area as a linear invert with no 1-sun clip in the kernel.

concept:spec-deferred.title: Missing physics is not a finding
concept:spec-deferred.recommend: Do not treat missing clouds, spectral atmosphere, umbra, wrinkles, or daytime fold as later results. They were left out on purpose.

concept:hand-625.note: can we do a second calc at a more reasonable size, 9square meter
concept:hand-625.title: Checked example (625 km, 55 m)
concept:hand-625.recommend: Accept 0.11 W/m² ideal (0.074 estimated) into a 5.8 km patch as the calibration point. If that scale feels wrong, stop before we draw or sweep the grid.
